case_studies.name: Riya
case_studies.profile_summary: High-achieving CS student worried about standing out in competitive tech region

challenges: Competition from local tech talent (Microsoft/Amazon employees' kids)
academic_profile.concern: Would get overlooked among peers aiming at local tech giants

strategy_applied: Identified unique angles to stand out

outcomes.lesson: Even strong students need strategic positioning in competitive regions

insights_for_agent: Geographic competition matters - students in tech hubs face stiffer competition
Strong academics alone aren't enough at top schools
Need to differentiate CS students in highly competitive markets
First-generation or unique background can be a differentiator
Regional counseling helps identify blind spots

college_fit_indicators.target_schools: Top public CS programs (Berkeley, CMU, UIUC)
college_fit_indicators.safety_schools: Strong state schools with CS (UW, Georgia Tech)

case_studies.name: Maya
case_studies.profile_summary: Brilliant student with transcript blemishes and scattered extracurriculars

challenges: Blemishes on transcript (poor grades in some classes)
Lack of focus in extracurricular activities list
academic_profile.parent_concern: Admissions officers might miss her potential

strategy_applied: Help craft narrative around her strengths

outcomes.lesson: Holistic review means blemishes can be overcome with strong narrative

insights_for_agent: Transcript imperfections don't disqualify strong students
Soft skills (debate, collaboration) matter at holistic schools
Narrative/essays can compensate for academic weaknesses
Schools doing holistic review value debate and intellectual engagement
Focus and consistency in extracurriculars matters, but depth > breadth

college_fit_indicators.key_factor: Holistic review schools > test-score focused schools
college_fit_indicators.reach_schools: Liberal arts colleges known for holistic review (Amherst, Williams)

case_studies.name: Ashley
case_studies.profile_summary: Aspiring doctor who used healthcare internship to build authentic college essay

experience.impact: Became cornerstone of successful college application

strategy_applied: Sought authentic internship in field of interest
Used internship story in college essays

outcomes.essay_impact: Internship story was cornerstone of application

insights_for_agent: Internships in major of interest strongly help applications
Real-world shadowing/research looks better than generic volunteering
Pre-med students need meaningful healthcare experience to stand out
Essay quality improves dramatically with authentic experiences
Medical research experience valuable for competitive pre-med admissions
Admissions officers want to see genuine passion through concrete action

college_fit_indicators.reach_schools: Pre-med programs at top schools (Johns Hopkins, Duke, Penn)
college_fit_indicators.target_schools: Strong pre-med programs at good universities
college_fit_indicators.key_schools_for_premd: Consider schools strong in medical outcomes, not just prestige

case_studies.name: Arjun
case_studies.profile_summary: CS student who secured ML startup internship to differentiate profile
strategy_applied: PathIvy matched with targeted ML startup

outcomes.lesson: Specialized internships in major of interest stand out

insights_for_agent: ML/AI experience increasingly important for CS admissions
Startup experience looks better than large tech company (shows real impact)
GitHub projects + internships = strong CS profile
CS students need 'proof of passion' through real projects
ML internships particularly valuable (competitive advantage)
Top CS programs expect technical depth, not just coursework

college_fit_indicators.major_specific_strategy: CS students must show passion through projects/research

case_studies.name: Brianna
case_studies.profile_summary: Budding entrepreneur who secured startup incubator internship

experience.impact: Helped secure admission to top business school

outcomes.lesson: Business schools value hands-on entrepreneurial experience

insights_for_agent: Business school admissions value entrepreneurial experience
Startup incubator experience > business camp
Fundraising/business model knowledge impressive for admissions
Leadership in business context highly valued
Real business problems > case study competitions
Demonstrating business acumen through action critical

college_fit_indicators.key_factor: Business schools want entrepreneurs, not just good grades

case_studies.name: David
case_studies.profile_summary: Politically inclined student with focus on congressional redistricting

differentiation.strategy: Deep focus on one policy area
differentiation.ethos_statement: Strong personal statement about political values

outcomes.lesson: Deep subject focus + publications highly impressive

insights_for_agent: Deep focus in one area beats many shallow activities
Published research is major admission boost
Political engagement + research shows serious commitment
Ethos statement critical for students with strong political views
Ivy League values intellectual depth and scholarly contribution
Activism + research is powerful combination

college_fit_indicators.reach_schools: Ivy League (Dartmouth, Cornell, Duke, Princeton, Yale)
college_fit_indicators.key_insight: Top schools want to see scholarly contribution, not just activities

case_studies.name: Sarah
case_studies.profile_summary: Student interested in intersection of humanities and technology

differentiation.strategy: Found unique angle at discipline intersection

insights_for_agent: Interdisciplinary interests can be stronger differentiator than pure CS
Tech + humanities combo increasingly valued
Shows breadth and intellectual curiosity
Digital humanities, HCI, ethics in AI are growing fields
Students with dual interests may find unique niche

college_fit_indicators.reach_schools: Schools strong in both tech and humanities (MIT, Stanford, CMU, Yale)
college_fit_indicators.target_schools: Universities with strong liberal arts + CS
college_fit_indicators.schools_to_consider: Consider schools with strong CS + humanities programs

case_studies.name: Vietnamese-American Student
case_studies.profile_summary: Strong academics but lacked standout extracurriculars; overcame through strategic positioning
case_studies.challenge: No major leadership positions, awards, or research experience despite strong academics
strategy_applied: Identified global perspective as unique angle
Crafted compelling personal story about overcoming adversity

outcomes.target: UPenn Huntsman Program (dual degree IR/Business, one of most competitive)
outcomes.timeline: Transformation in just a few months
outcomes.lesson: Strategic narrative can overcome ordinary extracurriculars

insights_for_agent: Perfect grades/test scores aren't enough without differentiation
Personal narrative and adversity overcome is crucial
First-gen/immigrant perspective valuable for admissions
Dual-degree programs (Huntsman, etc.) prefer strategic applicants
Global perspective + international interests help at competitive schools
Leadership growth narrative more valuable than early leadership
Cultural background + global interests strong combination

college_fit_indicators.reach_schools: UPenn Huntsman, Yale Jackson, Duke Sanford (dual degree IR programs)
college_fit_indicators.demographic_advantage: Immigrant background valuable at competitive universities

case_studies.name: East Asian Female Student
case_studies.profile_summary: Strong academics with exceptional music achievement and tech innovation

academic_profile.coursework: Rigorous but not exceptional for her school

extracurriculars.recognition: Performed at Carnegie Hall Winner's Recital

case_studies.challenge: Applied as senior (no time for profile changes before apps)

outcomes.lesson: Diverse accomplishments (music + STEM + service) can overcome time constraints

insights_for_agent: Carnegie Hall level music achievement is major differentiator
Female STEM students should leverage music/arts if accomplished
Founding tech-for-good non-profit is powerful combination
Research experience in natural sciences valuable
Asian American students face higher bar - need true distinction
Combining arts + STEM shows well-rounded intellectual
Service component (nursing home volunteering) shows character

college_fit_indicators.demographic_context: Asian American female in STEM - need extra distinction
college_fit_indicators.key_advantage: Exceptional achievement in either music or tech alone; this student has both

case_studies.name: Student with Cultural Travel Experience
case_studies.major: Liberal Arts / Economics / Pre-Med (depends on region)
case_studies.profile_summary: Student from region without college-going culture; differentiated through travel narrative

background.challenge: Peers don't pursue highly selective colleges
background.initial_profile: Not unique, especially at highly selective institutions
background.test_scores: A bit low relative to target schools

experience.key_differentiator: Significant family travel for cultural enrichment

strategy_applied: Leveraged travel experience as positioning strategy
Connected cultural exploration to intellectual curiosity

outcomes.lesson: Unique experience (travel, cultural learning) can overcome test score gaps

insights_for_agent: First-generation and region-of-origin can be strong differentiators
International exposure/travel shows initiative and global mindedness
Cultural learning narrative resonates with admissions officers
Can overcome moderate test scores with compelling narrative
Initiative to pursue learning outside school is impressive
First-gen from non-college-going region is advantage at some schools
Moderate test scores OK if narrative is compelling enough

college_fit_indicators.schools_preferring_firstgen: Many selective schools prioritize first-gen with compelling narratives
college_fit_indicators.note: Test scores less critical with strong narrative + first-gen status

what_admissions_officers_value: Depth in one area over breadth in many
Demonstrated passion in major of interest
what_doesn't_work: Spreading too thin across many activities
Essays that don't show who student is

cs_students: GitHub portfolio or published work helpful
Startup experience valued over corporate internships
stem_students: Show genuine curiosity, not just grades
liberal_arts_students: Depth in major + breadth in interests
Holistic review favors narrative + soft skills

first_generation: Strong narrative about family background essential
Narrative can offset moderate test scores
asian_american: Need true distinction (not just high grades)
international: Limited US activities OK, depth in home country matters

college_selection_wisdom: Top students need reach schools (where you're below 75th percentile)
Target schools should be middle 50% fit (25-75th percentile)
Safety schools need acceptance rate > 60% + good fit
Holistic review schools value narrative; test-score schools don't
Geographic competition varies (CA, NY, MA more competitive)
Regional public schools often undervalued (are actually great)
Specialized dual-degree programs (Huntsman, etc.) have specific values
